title: Why Is the Sky Blue?
summary: Why is the sky blue and not purple or white? Sunlight, tiny air molecules and a surprise about sunsets on Mars.

beats.text: Why is the sky blue? It isn't paint, and it isn't the ocean reflecting.
Sunlight looks white, but it's really every color of the rainbow mixed together.
To reach your eyes, that light has to crash through miles of air.
Quick guess! Which color gets bounced around the sky the most?
beats.reveal: Blue! Blue light gets scattered several times more than red.

beats.text: Blue light travels in short, choppy waves. Red light travels in long, lazy ones.
Tiny air molecules scatter the short blue waves in every direction, so blue reaches you from the whole sky.
At sunset, light travels through much more air. Most of the blue is scattered away, and reds are left.
Bonus fact: on Mars it's the other way round. The day sky looks dusty orange, and sunsets look blue!

visual.text: On Mars, the sunset is blue!
